page: Microsoft Azure D8alds_v6 is an x86_64 server instance powered by an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor running at 3.7 GHz. It features 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 4 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The memory configuration is 16.0 GB, providing 2.0 GB of RAM per core, which represents a lower memory-to-CPU ratio. The instance includes 472 GB of local storage and is capable of utilizing Premium Storage.

Benchmark results indicate strong single-core performance, with stress-ng single-core and Geekbench single-core scores placing in the top 25%. Text processing is a notable strength, achieving a top-tier rating in the top 10% of benchmarks. Multi-core CPU performance, Redis SET operations, and static web serving throughput fall within the average range. However, memory bandwidth for large uncached blocks is a relative bottleneck, scoring in the bottom 25%.

Given its dedicated compute resources and 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, this instance offers qualitative cost efficiency for compute-bound tasks that do not require massive memory footprints. The inclusion of 472 GB of local storage adds value for workloads requiring fast local scratch space. It is well-suited for single-threaded applications, text processing pipelines, web serving, and lightweight compilation tasks, though it is less optimal for memory-intensive databases or large-scale LLM inference.
description: Microsoft Azure D8alds_v6 is an x86_64 virtual machine powered by a 3.7 GHz AMD EPYC 9V74 processor. It features 8 dedicated vCPUs across 4 physical cores, 16.0 GB of system memory, and 472 GB of local storage. The server exhibits strong single-core CPU and text processing performance, with Geekbench single-core and text processing benchmarks ranking in the top 25% and top 10% respectively. However, its 2.0 GB of memory per core and weak large-block memory read bandwidth represent key hardware tradeoffs. This instance is qualitatively cost-effective for compute-focused workloads with moderate memory requirements, such as web serving, text processing, and software compilation, while remaining less suitable for memory-heavy databases or large language model inference.
